title: JSON
description: Learn about JSON encoding, decoding, struct tags, and streaming with Encoder/Decoder in Go
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## JSON

stdlib `json.dumps` / `json.loads` with `separators` when compact output must match Go.

exercises.title: Marshal a Struct
exercises.description: Define a Person struct with Name (string) and Age (int). Create a Person value and use json.Marshal to convert it to JSON. Print the resulting JSON bytes as a string.
hints: Use json.dumps with compact separators

exercises.title: Unmarshal JSON
exercises.description: Define a Person struct with Name and Age fields. Unmarshal the JSON string `{"Name":"Bob","Age":25}` into a Person variable. Print the Name and Age.
hints: p Person declares the variable
err := json.Unmarshal(jsonData, &p) decodes JSON into the struct
Pass a pointer to the variable so Unmarshal can modify it

exercises.title: JSON Struct Tags
exercises.description: Define a User struct with fields FirstName, LastName, and BirthYear. Use JSON struct tags to rename them to first_name, last_name, and birth_year in the JSON output. Marshal a User value and print the result.
hints: tag syntax: FirstName string `json:"first_name"`
Struct tags are enclosed in backticks
json.Marshal respects struct tags for field names

exercises.title: Omit Empty Tag
exercises.description: Define a Config struct with Server (string), Port (int), and Debug (bool). Use struct tags so that empty fields (zero values) are omitted from JSON output. Marshal a Config with only Server set and print.
hints: Add ,omitempty after the tag name: `json:"server,omitempty"`
Zero values are: empty string, 0, false
omitempty skips fields that have zero values

exercises.title: Marshal/Unmarshal Round Trip
exercises.description: Define a Product struct with ID (int), Name (string), and Price (float64). Marshal a Product to JSON, then unmarshal it back into a new variable. Print both values to verify the round trip preserved all data.
hints: data, _ := json.Marshal(original) converts to JSON bytes
recovered Product; json.Unmarshal(data, &recovered) decodes back
fmt.Printf uses %v for struct printing
exercises.solution:
import json
p={"id":1,"name":"Laptop","price":999.99}
j=json.dumps(p,separators=(",",":"))
r=json.loads(j)
def fmt(x): return "{"+str(x["id"])+" "+x["name"]+" "+f'{x["price"]:.2f}'+"}"
print("Original:",fmt(p))
print("Recovered:",fmt(r))

exercises.title: JSON with Nested Structs
exercises.description: Define an Address struct (Street, City) and a User struct (Name string, Address Address). Marshal a User with nested Address to JSON. Print the result showing the nested structure.
hints: Address struct needs Street string and City string fields
User struct embeds Address as a field (not a pointer)
json.Marshal handles nested structs automatically

exercises.title: JSON Encoder
exercises.description: Use json.NewEncoder with bytes.Buffer to encode a slice of Person values. Print the resulting JSON. This is useful for writing JSON to files or HTTP responses.
hints: buf bytes.Buffer; enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
enc.Encode(people) writes JSON to the buffer
Encode adds a trailing newline, use strings.TrimSpace to remove it

exercises.title: JSON RawMessage
exercises.description: Use json.RawMessage to defer parsing of a nested JSON field. Define a LogEntry struct with Level (string) and Data (json.RawMessage). Unmarshal a JSON object and print Level and the raw Data as a string.
hints: json.RawMessage is a []byte that holds raw JSON without parsing
After Unmarshal, Data will contain the raw JSON of the nested object
Print it with string(l.Data)

exercises.title: JSON Decoder
exercises.description: Use json.NewDecoder with a bytes.Buffer containing a JSON array of Person values. Decode each Person one at a time using dec.Decode() in a loop. Print each person's Name and Age.
hints: buf bytes.Buffer; buf.WriteString(jsonData); dec := json.NewDecoder(&buf)
Use a for loop with dec.Decode(&p); if err == io.EOF { break }
json.Decoder is great for streaming data from files or network connections
